thread:
maria: Heads up — I'm seeing a ~15% p99 tail latency regression on INT8 AWQ weight-only workloads after yesterday's kernel-routing reorder deploy. p50 looks unchanged. Anyone else noticed this?
cheng: pinging perf CI, any traces yet?
maria: attached a short flame and kernel chooser log. Key snippet: 
```
[KernelChooser] model=gptx awq_group=32 seq=128 selected=awq_packed_v2 fallback=scalar_unpacked reason=unaligned_pack
kernels: awq_packed_v2 185us/op; scalar_unpacked 320us/op; weighted_count=24
request: batch=4 avg_seq=120
```:eyes:
julian: if the chooser falls back to scalar_unpacked that's a massive per-token cost hit. Two quick hypotheses: (1) packing alignment / slab boundary mismatch causing unpack path, (2) batching heuristic creating mixed group sizes that don't match packed-kernel vector width.
tara: any change in default group-size or alignment in the deploy? I remember the kernel reordering DID change the policy that picks pref_pack when mem pressure high.
maria: deploy touched kernel_priority: [awq_packed_v2, awq_packed_v1, awq_scalar] and also changed prefer_shorter_batch=true -> this increased micro-batches, so we see more mixed group sizes.
cheng: can you run the microbench that toggles group sizes? please include --trace-kernel-chooser output. Use: `./tools/bench --model gptx-awq --seq 128 --batch 4 --group 16,32,64 --pack yes --trace-kernel-chooser`
maria: did a quick run, results: 
```
group=16 -> p99=172ms kernel=awq_packed_v2 hit=98%
group=32 -> p99=196ms kernel=awq_packed_v2 hit=72% fallback=scalar_unpacked 28%
group=64 -> p99=318ms kernel=scalar_unpacked hit=65% pack_hit=35%
```
Looks like larger groups increase fallback.
julian: that suggests packing overhead + an alignment check in the kernel falls back when the combined packed buffer wouldn't be contiguous. Could be our slab allocator or the prefetcher adding padding.
tara: also remember AWQ has group-size-dependent kernel implementations (group==32 optimized lanes). If our packer is choosing group-size based on quant calibration output, small changes in calibration can flip group-size -> kernel variant.
maria: interesting — we ran calibrations last week (AWQ opts) which changed per-layer group_stride slightly. That might have changed pack alignment.
cheng: I want telemetry: add counters for (pack_attempts, pack_failures_reason=[unaligned, mem_pressure, fallback_kernel_mismatch]). If we can count how many requests trigger scalar_unpacked we can correlate to p99.
julian: quick mitigation: in runtime, prefer_packed_kernels fallback threshold -> only fallback if scalar_unpacked is >2x slower, otherwise force pack. But that risks correctness/perf if packing introduces extra copies.
tara: I'd rather adjust batching heuristic: avoid mixing group sizes inside a batch. If we coalesce by group_size at request scheduling, we should increase packed hit-rate without changing single-request behavior.
maria: agreed — coalescing sounds lower risk. But we need to measure cost of extra queuing latency.
cheng: experiment plan: (A) run bench with coalescing scheduler patch, (B) run with prefer_packed_kernels=true and telemetry, (C) re-run AWQ calibrate with group_hint=32/64 to see quality/perf impact. We'll compare p50/p95/p99 and pack_hit %.
maria: also captured a trace that shows KV cache eviction interacting: for some long chats the KV cache pages get moved and allocator returns non-contiguous backing, which breaks our packer assumption of contiguous weight blocks. Trace shows `kv_cache_eviction=1` around time of pack fallback.
julian: oh that's important — eviction + allocator fragmentation -> unaligned weights. Two options: force compaction before packing (expensive) or make packer handle discontiguous segments by doing local copies into an aligned staging buffer (cheaper but extra copy).
tara: staging buffer seems pragmatic and contained. Let's benchmark copy cost vs scalar kernel slow path.
ci-bot: deploy status — rollback window ends in 6h (deploy id: rwd-2024-06-14-ker-reroute).
maria: action items: 
- julian: add packer telemetry + fallback reason counters (ETA 3h)
- cheng: run the three bench runs and upload traces to /tmp/perf/1714567890 (ETA 2h)
- tara: prototype staging-buffer fallback in packer, microbench (ETA 6h)
- maria: watch CI and revert deploy if p99 still >10% reg (will decide at 6h) :thumbsup:
julian: also opening a perf PR to log pack-alignment stats in traces.
cheng: noted — will post bench output once done.
maria: thanks all — let's sync in #eng-runtime after we have bench numbers. :coffee:
